lines.trans: Today is the very best day of my life.
Today my daughter smiled at me for the first time.
Honestly, she smiled, I am not lying!
Literally a minute ago she was smiling at me.
Nothing special, she is simply falling asleep.
Let's wait, maybe she will smile again?
Viktor Petrovich, you have returned to us again!
And all of us already thought you had left.

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait for, to live to see', paired with 'дожидаться'.

examples.text: Я дождусь ответа.
examples.trans: I will wait for an answer.

examples.text: Я всё равно дождусь твоего ответа!
examples.trans: I will wait for your answer anyway!

examples.text: Я готов спокойно дождаться решения суда.
examples.trans: I am ready to wait calmly for the court decision.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such a thing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Даже не надейтесь, не дождётесь такого!
examples.trans: Do not even hope for it, you will never see the day!

examples.text: Не мог я ей отказать в такой ситуации.
examples.trans: I could not refuse her in such a situation.

examples.text: Так я тебе отдам в два раза дешевле.
examples.trans: I will give it to you for half the price.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы очень рады снова видеть вас, шеф.
examples.trans: We are very glad to see you again, Chef.

examples.text: Она очень серьёзно у нас болеет.
examples.trans: She is very seriously sick.

examples.text: Огузок, почему ты снова опаздываешь на смену?
examples.trans: Oguzok, why are you late for your shift again?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('glad').

examples.text: Мы очень рады снова видеть вас, шеф.
examples.trans: We are very glad to see you again, Chef.

examples.text: Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Она рада.
examples.trans: She's glad.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Мы очень рады снова видеть вас, шеф.
examples.trans: We are very glad to see you again, Chef.

examples.text: Не хочу тебя больше видеть, прощай.
examples.trans: I do not want to see you anymore, goodbye.

examples.text: Я вижу машинку.
examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

examples.text: Прости, что я тебе тогда не сказала.
examples.trans: Forgive me for not telling you back then.

examples.text: Тогда я предлагаю тебе честное пари.
examples.trans: Then I propose an honest bet to you.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

examples.text: Он быстро едет.
examples.trans: He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Буквально минуту назад она мне улыбалась.
examples.trans: Literally a minute ago she was smiling at me.

examples.text: Ничего особенного, она просто засыпает.
examples.trans: Nothing special, she is simply falling asleep.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

examples.text: Всё, иди спокойно работай и не плачь.
examples.trans: That is all, go work calmly and do not cry.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, я не буду у вас работать.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, I will not work for you.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'дельник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'slackers' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда быстро за работу, бездельники!
examples.trans: Then get back to work quickly, slackers!

examples.text: Тихо на кухне, бездельники!
examples.trans: Quiet in the kitchen, idlers!

examples.text: Бездельники! Огрызки! Что вы делаете?
examples.trans: Slackers! Scraps! What are you doing?
